title: Applied ML Eval Harness: Prompt Sets, Model Onboarding, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standard operating procedures for the Applied ML eval ecosystem: the eval harness onboarding flow, prompt-set authoring & benchmarking standards, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and the regression triage workflow. Aim: detect quality regressions early, standardize comparisons across models/quantizations, and minimize customer-impacting regressions during model/infra changes.

Goals
-----
- Provide a single, repeatable onboarding and evaluation flow for new models and model variants.
- Maintain high signal-to-noise for regressions by standardizing prompt-sets, metrics, and thresholds.
- Ensure quantization recommendations include quality vs cost tradeoffs and an automated gating mechanism.
- Define a clear triage and rollback path for detected regressions.

Scope
-----
Applies to: new model onboarding (open checkpoints and curated weights), model variant releases (quantized builds, distilled/optimized variants), and infra/runtime changes that could affect output quality. Not covered: exploratory research experiments that are not intended for serving.

Ownership & Roles
----------------
- Applied ML (primary): build and operate the eval harness, own prompt-set catalog, run periodic benchmarks.
- Serving Runtime (secondary): provide perf/latency metrics and help reproduce issues in the runtime.
- Product/Platform: prioritize model rollouts and define customer-facing SLAs.
- On-call & SRE: lead regression incident response if customer-impacting.
- Data Privacy & Security: approve any customer data used for evals.

Key Definitions
---------------
- Eval harness: automated system that runs prompt-sets across model versions/quantization profiles and produces metrics, diffs, and artifacts for review.
- Prompt set: curated list of prompts with expected outputs or metrics used for regression detection and quality benchmarks.
- Regression: any statistically significant degradation (see thresholds) in a guardrail metric versus baseline.
- Quantization profile: YAML description of the quantization method, expected FP-equivalent, and performance/cost tradeoffs.

SLOs & Thresholds (guardrails)
-------------------------------
- Aggregate semantic accuracy (task-dependent): no more than 2.0 percentage points drop vs pinned baseline for critical tasks.
- Toxicity / safety regression: zero allowable increase in high-confidence toxic labels for customer-facing datasets; any increase triggers block.
- Latency P95 for inference: must stay within 10% of baseline unless explicitly approved.
- Token-level perplexity (where applicable): relative increase <= 5%.
- Human-eval degradation (A/B preference): a statistically significant preference (p<0.05) for baseline over candidate is a failure.

Eval Harness Onboarding Checklist
--------------------------------
1. Create a model entry in the eval catalog: name, architecture, commit/tag, checkpoint URL, expected vocab/tokenizer, and responsible owner.
2. Add metadata: target use-cases, expected cost profile, and baseline model to compare against.
3. Register quantization profiles to test (see Quantization Profiles section).
4. Add required prompt-sets (see Prompt Set standards).
5. Run the standard harness jobs: unit sanity, regression battery, safety scans, and performance benchmarks.
6. Review automated reports and commit artifacts (diffs, example failures, metric trends).
7. Approve model for canary if all checks pass; otherwise iterate on prompt/label adjustments or model variant.

CLI / Example commands (eval harness)
------------------------------------
- Run full evaluation locally (dev harness):
  ./eval-harness run --model-tag v1.2.0 --profiles standard,quantized --prompt-sets core-benchmarks,safety-smoke --output-dir /tmp/eval-v1.2.0

- Submit batch job (k8s):
  evalctl submit --model v1.2.0 --prompt-sets core-benchmarks,safety-smoke --profiles standard --notify @applied-ml

Prompt Sets & Benchmarking Standards
-----------------------------------
- Prompt set types:
  - Core benchmarks: task-specific suites for retrieval, summarization, QA, code, and dialog.
  - Safety smoke: short set to detect high-confidence unsafe outputs.
  - Edge-cases: long-tail prompts collected from customer incidents and fuzzing.
  - Regression canonical: golden prompts used to detect subtle regressions across releases.

Authoring rules:
- Each prompt must include: id, description, input, expected metrics (exact match, n-gram overlap, embedding similarity thresholds), and tags (task, sensitivity).
- Avoid leaking customer PII; use synthetic or consented examples only.
- Maintain a prompt-set owner and version history.

Benchmark execution cadence:
- Nightly runs: core-benchmarks across pinned baselines and current main.
- Pre-release: full battery for each candidate build.
- On-demand: when infra or runtime changes are suspected to affect quality.

Model Onboarding Template (required fields)
-----------------------------------------
- Model name: string
- Model family & architecture: (e.g., LLaMA2-70B, transformer variant)
- Checkpoint URL / digest: string
- Tokenizer & vocab: string
- Baseline model: string (pinned)
- Responsible owner: name/email
- Target use-cases & excluded use-cases: list
- Quantization profiles to validate: list
- Safety notes & provenance: string
- Expected perf profile (tokens/s, memory) and initial SLOs: string

Quality Guardrails & Metrics
---------------------------
Guardrails break down into automated signals and human review triggers:
- Automated signals:
  - Metric diffs across prompt-sets (semantic accuracy, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, embed-similarity).
  - Safety classifier deltas (toxicity, hallucination heuristics).
  - Latency and memory regression detection.
- Human review triggers:
  - Any safety classifier increase flagged as high-confidence.
  - >2% absolute drop in semantic accuracy on critical prompt-sets.
  - Reproducible high-impact customer example failing.

Quantization Profiles (guidelines + example)
-------------------------------------------
Guidance:
- Profiles must declare: name, method (e.g., fp16, int8, awq, nf4), intended tradeoff (latency/cost vs quality), and recommended use-cases.
- Always test a quantized candidate against the same prompt-sets and baselines.
- Maintain a gold-standard unquantized artifact for comparison.
- For int8/AWQ, add stress tests for long-context generation to detect KV-cache related regressions.

Example profile YAML (store under quantization-profiles catalog):
---
profile_name: awq-int8-fast
method: awq
bit_width: 8
expected_equivalent_fp: fp16
intended_use_cases: ["chat","short-completions"]
notes: "Aggressive per-block quantization optimized for latency on A100 and H100; validate long-context outputs."
---
(When saving in catalog, include metrics from standardized run: semantic_accuracy, latency_p95, memory_mb, cost_estimate_per_1M_tokens.)

Regression Triage Playbook
-------------------------
1. Detection: automated job flags metric(s) crossing thresholds. Alert to #applied-ml-regressions Slack and create a Jira.
2. Triage & Repro: owner runs eval-harness locally with pinned baseline and candidate to reproduce. Include exact seed, prompt-set IDs, and environment (runtime/CPU/GPU driver).
3. Categorize: a) model-only quality regression, b) quantization-induced, c) runtime/inference bug, d) dataset/metric drift.
4. Immediate mitigation paths:
   - If regression is safety-critical: block rollout and notify security & product; start hotfix/candidate rollback.
   - If regression is model-specific and minor: pin baseline for affected customers and schedule fix.
   - If runtime-induced: revert rollout or apply runtime patch; collaborate with serving-runtime SRE.
5. Root cause analysis: produce a postmortem-like triage note with repro steps, diffs, failing prompt examples, and metric plots.
6. Remediation & validation: implement fix (retrain, re-quantize, kernel fix), run full harness, and obtain approval before redeploy.
7. Communicate: update stakeholders (product, CS, and impacted customers) with timeline and mitigation steps.

Example triage checklist (short)
- Repro locally? (yes/no)
- Affects safety? (yes/no)
- Affects >X% of core-benchmark? (yes/no; specify X)
- Quick rollback available? (yes/no)
- Owner assigned & ETA: name / 72h

Postmortem & Continuous Improvement
----------------------------------
- For all regressions that breached thresholds, create a lightweight postmortem within 5 business days documenting root cause, fixes applied, and preventive actions (e.g., adding prompts to the regression canonical set).
- Periodically (quarterly) review prompt-set coverage and update to include new customer failure modes.
- Maintain a changelog for quantization profiles and map them to observed metric deltas over time.

Operational Notes & Artifact Storage
----------------------------------
- All harness outputs (raw logs, model outputs for failing prompts, evaluation metrics, plots) are stored in the eval-artifacts S3 bucket under /models/{model-name}/{tag}/{run-timestamp}/.
- Attach the S3 link to the Jira for traceability.
- Long-term storage: retain artifacts for 365 days by default; reduce retention for ephemeral dev runs.

Related pages & references
-------------------------
- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quantization best-practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Regression triage examples: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-regression-triage-playbook-2026

Appendix: Quick Scripting snippets
--------------------------------
- Generate a CSV of failing prompt ids and examples:
  python tools/extract_failures.py --run s3://eval-artifacts/models/llama2-70b/v1.2.0/2026-11-19 --threshold 0.02 --out failures.csv

- Re-run a single prompt with deterministic seed:
  ./eval-harness run --model-tag v1.2.0 --prompt-ids prompt-1234 --seed 42 --output-dir /tmp/repro
